Cited reasons do not apply to unrestricted transport. An affine closure 'ES(n) ⇒ ES(an+b) on a class', used with strong induction (ES(p) from ES((p−b)/a), all smaller n assumed), is a recursive procedure of depth ≍ log p, not a finite formal run, so B1 Thm M/Mordell–Schinzel do not cover it. T1 does not bind solvability either, because ES(m²) holds by scaling (but a transport that preserves Type I/II-ness still meets T1). Not refuted. Real constraints: the map must transform an ARBITRARY solution of n (no integral correspondence U_n ⇢ U_{an+b} is known), privacy (affine shifts do not transport divisors), and 4-specificity (8/131 fails). Open, but there is no handle.
